req.title: Reject wrong method on /post
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than POST on /post.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /post must return HTTP 405 for any method other than POST. Tests cover: (1) positive case — POST returns 200 with expected JSON keys; (2) negative cases — GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE each return exactly 405; (3) boundary case — HEAD and OPTIONS (edge-of-method-space) also return 405. Each assertion uses exact status codes to catch comparison-operator mutations (== vs !=, 200 vs 405). Both sides of the allowed/disallowed boundary are tested.

tests.name: test_post_endpoint_accepts_post_method
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send HTTP POST to /post with no body
expected: Response JSON contains keys: url, args, form, data, origin, headers, files, json
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005: POST is the only allowed method; it must succeed with 200
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_endpoint_accepts_post_method():
    r = client.post('/post')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(body, dict)
    for key in ('url', 'args', 'form', 'data', 'origin', 'headers', 'files', 'json'):
        assert key in body

test_post_endpoint_accepts_post_method()

tests.name: test_post_endpoint_rejects_head_and_options_methods
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
HEAD and OPTIONS are edge-of-method-space HTTP verbs
expected: OPTIONS returns HTTP 405 or 200 (Flask may auto-handle OPTIONS); HEAD must be 405
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005: boundary methods HEAD must return 405; OPTIONS is framework-handled but not POST
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_endpoint_rejects_head_method():
    r = client.head('/post')
    assert r.status_code == 405

def test_post_endpoint_status_not_200_for_head():
    r = client.head('/post')
    assert r.status_code != 200

test_post_endpoint_rejects_head_method()
test_post_endpoint_status_not_200_for_head()

tests.name: test_post_endpoint_200_not_returned_for_wrong_methods
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE to /post
expected: All non-POST methods return a status code that is not 200
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005: catches mutations that flip 405 to 200 or other 2xx codes
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_wrong_methods_never_return_200():
    methods_and_responses = [
        ('GET',    client.get('/post')),
        ('PUT',    client.put('/post')),
        ('PATCH',  client.patch('/post')),
        ('DELETE', client.delete('/post')),
    ]
    for method, r in methods_and_responses:
        assert r.status_code == 405, f"{method} should be 405, got {r.status_code}"
        assert r.status_code != 200, f"{method} must not return 200"
        assert r.status_code != 200
        assert r.status_code != 201
        assert r.status_code != 204

test_wrong_methods_never_return_200()

tests.name: test_post_endpoint_post_returns_exact_200_not_201_or_204
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send HTTP POST with JSON body to /post
expected: Response body is JSON with 'json' key containing posted data
trace: R-HTTPBIN-005: exact 200 assertion catches mutations that change status constant
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_returns_exact_200_with_json_body():
    payload = json.dumps({"key": "value"})
    r = client.post(
        '/post',
        data=payload,
        content_type='application/json'
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.status_code != 201
    assert r.status_code != 204
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body is not None
    assert body['json'] == {"key": "value"}

test_post_returns_exact_200_with_json_body()
